entries.note: Only explicit test-mode startup creates the stdin reader. Commands enqueue ordinary SDL key/mouse/text/focus events and expose read-only state/rendered snapshots. Pointer commands can set modifier state and wheel commands carry signed precise deltas plus inversion metadata to exercise production mouse reporting. It does not start a network listener or replace real file/session/game operations with fixtures. Tests clean their owned process; this remains separate from the agent desktop-action protocol. One command has a side effect beyond input: plugin (spec 106) loads a module into this window through re_app_plugin_load with the same three inputs the declaring lane will pass, so a real module is exercised in a real window before the declaration format exists; it is still only reachable through this opt-in channel. fileLinkCursor compares SDL_GetCursor with the real desktop-owned hand cursor, so a missing SDL_SetCursor call cannot pass by merely setting a desired-state flag. Input commands enqueue events; cursor checks wait for the subsequent rendered frame.

What a control's rectangle cannot say. The inspect payload reports controls, and a control's rectangle told a spec that a row existed and nothing about the strings inside it — so two strings drawn on top of each other was invisible to every test and obvious in a screenshot (2026-09-14). The draw list already holds the answer, so this reports it: every RE_CMD_TEXT of the last completed frame, its measured box, and the clip in force when it was emitted.

The clip is not an extra: it is what separates the two failures a spec wants to tell apart. Without it a label microui clipped reads as an overlap (the unclipped box runs under its neighbour) and a name elided to a stub reads as whole. Both boxes are reported — `x/y/w/h` is the string's full extent, `visible` is that intersected with the clip — so a spec says which it means: `visible == full` is "drawn whole", and two `visible` boxes intersecting is "drawn on top of each other".

The frame this reads is the LAST one: the list is reset in `re_draw_begin` and automation commands are handled between frames, so a caller that changes state must let a frame draw before asking.
